claim.evidence: ACIP C05:180 contains MYON MONGS PA verbatim and its Wylie agrees, myon mongs pa. The preceding root C05:179 has NYON MONGS and English Mental affliction; the commentary 180 translates the same first condition as mental affliction. The live glossary-tier entry nyon mongs pa attests mental affliction, and an exact myon mongs pa entry is absent. A targeted query excluding the unscanned C13 returns exactly two myon mongs rows, C05:180 and C16:759; the latter matches all three source fields byte for byte and is the same source re-ingested. The corrected prose search nyon mongs pa dang rab has zero non-C13 spine rows. Local digital text witnesses were read and hashed independently at folio marker @124B: SE5525M and SE05525M (SHA256 933d04e506d356a0deb8da05996778e1ef58a313255df981d45d224834c8f913) both read 'ZHEN, MYON MONGS PA'; the distinct SL05525N file (SHA256 12aca4d3a071d600b704761aa82568b7a09175cef62d25e2d3caf9d6b25c179f) reads 'ZHEN, NYON MONGS PA'. All are local digital copies titled DAM PA'I CHOS MNGON PA'I MDZOD KYI RNAM PAR BSHAD PA THAR LAM GSAL BYED, attributed to Rgyal ba Dge 'dun grub, under the campaign-worktree library/sungbum/Sungbum collection; exact paths, original line breaks and full passage quotes are preserved in local-witness-verification.json. The two SE filenames are identical bytes and not two independent witnesses. SL is a distinct digital reading, but publication independence has not been established and no manuscript or blockprint was inspected. The source spelling is therefore a LOW/PROBABLE editorial candidate, not a proven correction; the corpus remains untouched. The current errata register has no C05:178–180/MYON duplicate, and this is not a registered converter, heading, folio, footnote, row-spill or English-cap class.

rows.english: "Just what," one may ask, "do you mean when you mention types of deeds that are certain to ripen?" Those deeds are definite (will definitely ripen into a future experience) which involve any of the following: 1) fierce emotions, of either mental affliction or faith; 2) an object of special qualities--that is, deeds performed with respect to the Gems; 3) anything done on a continual basis; and 4) killing one's father or mother, even when this is done with meritorious intent.
